alerts-bot: [INC-2026-042] RESOLVED - Routing compile backlog caused transient 5xxs on hosted inference. Start: 2026-03-16T12:23:00Z, Resolved: 2026-03-16T12:39:00Z. Autoscaler fallback triggered, traffic routed to compatible model variants. Investigating root cause. Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-042 :white_check_mark:

alice (oncall): Confirmed - mitigation was the routing fallback policy. No data exfil or model integrity impact. Estimated ~14 minutes of elevated error rates for ~2% of requests in us-west-2.

ben (sre): Timeline I have for RCA notes: 12:22 — compile queue spike after a nightly model publish; 12:23 — autoscaler compile backlog hit threshold; 12:25 — routing fallback engaged; 12:39 — backlog drained and normal routing resumed. Collecting logs + kernel traces.

carmen (cs): Thanks. Need a short customer-facing summary we can send to affected accounts (top 10 + a general broadcast). Also need list of impacted customers and suggested SLA credit language. Who can draft?

alice (oncall): Draft below — short and neutral. Please edit for CS tone.

alice (oncall): "Hi <customer>, we experienced a brief disruption to hosted inference on 2026-03-16 between 12:23–12:39 UTC. Some requests returned errors or experienced increased latency during this window. Our automated routing fallback successfully routed traffic to compatible model variants; there was no exposure of customer data. We’ve implemented a fix to reduce compile queue buildup and will follow up with a targeted RCA shortly. If you received errors during that time we can assist with replaying requests or reviewing usage impact. — Redwood Inference Support"

carmen (cs): Nice — tightening a couple phrases for tone and next steps, and adding SLA credit proposal: 

carmen (cs): "Hi <customer>, we wanted to let you know about a short service disruption on 2026-03-16 between 12:23–12:39 UTC. During this window, a subset of requests to our hosted inference API returned errors or saw increased latency. Our automated fallback routed traffic to compatible model variants which restored service. We are confident there was no exposure of customer data.

We’ve applied a fix to prevent compilation queue buildup and are preparing a formal RCA with mitigation actions. If you were impacted, we can help replay requests or estimate token-level impact. For customers impacted by errors, we propose a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of affected invoice line items for the day; please reply if you’d prefer a different remediation.

We apologize for the disruption and are available to discuss further. — Redwood Customer Success"

elaine (legal): Wording looks good. Suggest removing "confident" (use definitive phrasing) and avoid implying guarantees. Recommend: "There was no exposure of customer data identified during our investigation."

carmen (cs): Good call. Updated: "There was no exposure of customer data identified during our investigation." Also adding a short FAQ line: "How do I know if I was impacted? We'll include a summary with request counts and errors per route if you ask us."

derek (product): Can we add one sentence about permanent mitigations? e.g., "We’re adding a pre-compile admission control and tighter autoscaler thresholds to prevent recurrence." Keep it high-level.

ben (sre): Fine to include that — RFC/patchs are already in review. For the RCA I'll send a consolidated timeline + root cause (compile queue growth due to an unbounded concurrent compile loop after model publish) and the planned fixes: pre-compile admission, backpressure on publisher, and metrics/alerts tuned to detect queue growth earlier.

carmen (cs): Great. Plan: I will send the customer note to top 10 impacted accounts after legal thumbs-up and attach a short per-customer impact summary (error counts + token estimate). Also will post the updated message to the customer status mailing list for broader visibility.

elaine (legal): Thumbs-up on the revised language. Suggest CCing product/security for any direct responses that ask about internal processes.

carmen (cs): Will do. One ask: can SRE provide the per-account error counts by EOD so we can send notes today? @ben

ben (sre): I can get a CSV with per-account request/error counts + example request ids by 18:00 UTC.

alice (oncall): Also note for the postmortem: include the autoscaler config that allowed the compile backlog threshold to be reached; add reproduction steps for the Q/A team.

carmen (cs): Thanks everyone. Final ask: please react with :thumbsup: if you approve sending the customer note + proposed 10% credit to impacted accounts.

ben (sre): :thumbsup:

derek (product): :thumbsup:

elaine (legal): :thumbsup:

alice (oncall): :thumbsup:

carmen (cs): Sending to top 10 now, will post broadcast at 13:15 UTC with link to status page and attach per-account impact summaries when available. Closing thread for send confirmation.
